requirements.evidence: Contract met: enum app/Enums/CallMode.php:5-9, NoWaitingTicketsException extends RuntimeException (app/Exceptions/NoWaitingTicketsException.php:7), invokable action with the required signature (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:24-28). Queue row locked and is_active read from DB (CallNextTicket.php:30-37); waiting + queue filter (:73-74); ordering priority desc/issued_at/id (:77-81, :88); normal_only oldest first (:82-85); fairness looks at last 3 by called_at desc, id desc (:98-115); candidate re-lock and re-check of status (:41-51); only status/called_at/called_by_user_id set via Eloquent save (:53-56). Edge case gap: when fairness restricts to normals and the only waiting normal is claimed concurrently by Ticket::call(), the loop exhausts and throws NoWaitingTicketsException even though priority tickets are waiting (:86-88, :61-63).

conventions.evidence: Domain write in app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php, one class per use case, no service layer; reuses InactiveQueueException; PHPDoc on the public method (:17-23); docs/architecture.md:129-141 and docs/business-rules.md:3, :102-113, :131, :143 updated as required, and the CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry was added (CHANGELOG.md:21). Ships a Pest test file.

security.evidence: Authorization is out of scope (trusted caller per task.md). No mass assignment: attributes set individually (CallNextTicket.php:53-55); queries are fully parameterized; the queue state comes from a locked DB read, not from the passed model (:30-35). No weaknesses found.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php covers ordering, id tie-break, other queues, already called tickets, all three modes, all three NoWaitingTickets cases, fairness trigger/no-trigger/no-normal-waiting/priority_only ignore/priority_only counting/normal reset, inactive and stale queue, and the returned model state. However, the race test (:84-111) intercepts the first query whose bindings contain $top->id; with fresh ids the queue id and $top->id are both likely 1, so the hook can fire on the fairness/candidate SELECT (bindings [queue_id, status]) before selection rather than between selection and the row lock, so the skip path may not actually be exercised. getChanges()->toHaveKeys (:344) does not prove that only those columns changed.

simplicity.evidence: Lean, one action plus a small helper for fairness. The orderBy('issued_at')->orderBy('id') chain is repeated four times in candidateQuery (CallNextTicket.php:77-88) and the waiting-normal filter is duplicated between candidateQuery and shouldServeNormalFirst (:87 vs :111-115); minor duplication.

readability.evidence: Clear names (candidateQuery, shouldServeNormalFirst, lockedQueue), short methods, explanatory comment on the race skip (CallNextTicket.php:47-48), match expression per mode (:76-89). No dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Diff limited to the action, enum, exception, tests, the two required docs and CHANGELOG. No HTTP/Livewire/authorization added; no unrelated refactors.

issues.explanation: The race-simulation hook matches any tickets query whose bindings contain $top->id, which can also match the queue_id binding of the fairness/candidate SELECT (both ids are likely 1), so the ticket may be marked called before selection and the lock-and-re-check skip path is not reliably exercised.

When fairness restricts the candidate list to normals and those normals are concurrently claimed via Ticket::call(), the action throws NoWaitingTicketsException instead of falling back to the waiting priority tickets as the 'no normal waiting' rule implies.
Fairness history filters on status = called rather than only called_at, so it will silently ignore calls once later statuses (served, skipped) are introduced.
toHaveKeys on getChanges() only proves the three fields changed, not that no other write-once attribute changed.
The issued_at/id ordering chain and the normal-ticket filter are repeated across match arms and could be shared.

review.summary: Adds the CallNextTicket action with CallMode enum and NoWaitingTicketsException, implementing deterministic ordering, the three modes, three-call fairness, locked inactive-queue check and per-candidate lock/re-check, with docs, changelog and an extensive Pest suite. The implementation is correct and follows the conventions; the remaining points are a race test that may not exercise the path it targets and a narrow concurrency fallback gap in fairness mode, so I would approve with minor follow-ups.
